verses.zh: 第七年五月初十日，有以色列的几个长老来求问耶和华，坐在我面前。
verses.en: In the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth of the month,[NOTE:1] some of the elders[NOTE:2] of Israel came to seek[NOTE:3] the Lord, and they sat down in front of me.
notes: The date would be August 14th, 591 b.c. The seventh year is the seventh year of Jehoiachin’s exile.
Heb “men from the elders.”
See the note at 14:3.

verses.zh: 耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要告诉以色列的长老说，主耶和华如此说：你们来是求问我吗？主耶和华说：我指着我的永生起誓，我必不被你们求问。
verses.en: “Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel, and tell them: ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: Are you coming to seek me? As surely as I live, I will not allow you to seek me,[NOTE:1] declares the Sovereign Lord.’
notes: Or “I will not reveal myself to you.”

verses.zh: 人子啊，你要审问审问他们吗？你当使他们知道他们列祖那些可憎的事，
verses.en: Are you willing to pronounce judgment on them?[NOTE:1] Are you willing to pronounce judgment, son of man? Then confront them with the abominable practices of their fathers,
notes: Heb “will you judge.” Here the imperfect form of the verb is probably used with a desiderative nuance. Addressed to the prophet, “judge” means to warn of or pronounce God’s impending judgment.

verses.zh: 对他们说，主耶和华如此说：当日我拣选以色列，向雅各家的后裔起誓，在埃及地将自己向他们显现，说：我是耶和华―你们的　神。
verses.en: and say to them: “‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: On the day I chose Israel I swore[NOTE:1] to the descendants[NOTE:2] of the house of Jacob and made myself known to them in the land of Egypt. I swore[NOTE:3] to them, “I am the Lord your God.”
notes: Heb “I lifted up my hand.”
Heb “seed.”
Heb “I lifted up my hand.”

verses.zh: 那日我向他们起誓，必领他们出埃及地，到我为他们察看的流奶与蜜之地；那地在万国中是有荣耀的。
verses.en: On that day I swore[NOTE:1] to bring them out of the land of Egypt to a land that I had picked out[NOTE:2] for them, a land flowing with milk and honey,[NOTE:3] the most beautiful of all lands.
notes: Heb “I lifted up my hand to them.”
Or “searched out.” The Hebrew word is used to describe the activity of the spies in “spying out” the land of Canaan (Num 13-14); cf. KJV “I had espied for them.”

The phrase “a land flowing with milk and honey,” a figure of speech describing the land’s abundant fertility, occurs in v. 15 as well as Exod 3:8, 17; 13:5; 33:3; Lev 20:24; Num 13:27; Deut 6:3; 11:9; 26:9; 27:3; Josh 5:6; Jer 11:5; 32:23 (see also Deut 1:25; 8:7-9).

verses.zh: 我对他们说，你们各人要抛弃眼所喜爱那可憎之物，不可因埃及的偶像玷污自己。我是耶和华―你们的　神。
verses.en: I said to them, “Each of you must get rid of the detestable idols you keep before you,[NOTE:1] and do not defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt; I am the Lord your God.”
notes: Heb “each one, the detestable things of his eyes, throw away.” The Pentateuch does not refer to the Israelites worshiping idols in Egypt, but Josh 24:14 appears to suggest that they did so.

verses.zh: 他们却悖逆我，不肯听从我，不抛弃他们眼所喜爱那可憎之物，不离弃埃及的偶像。「我就说，我要将我的忿怒倾在他们身上，在埃及地向他们成就我怒中所定的。
verses.en: But they rebelled against me and refused to listen to me; no one got rid of their detestable idols,[NOTE:1] nor did they abandon the idols of Egypt. Then I decided to pour out[NOTE:2] my rage on them and fully vent my anger against them in the midst of the land of Egypt.
notes: Heb “each one, the detestable things of their eyes did not throw away.”
Heb “and I said/thought to pour out.”

verses.zh: 我却为我名的缘故没有这样行，免得我名在他们所住的列国人眼前被亵渎；我领他们出埃及地，在这列国人的眼前将自己向他们显现。
verses.en: I acted for the sake of my reputation,[NOTE:1] so that I would not be profaned before the nations among whom they lived,[NOTE:2] before whom I revealed myself by bringing them out of the land of Egypt.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “for the sake of my name.”
Heb “before the eyes of the nations in whose midst they were.”

Heb “to whom I made myself known before their eyes to bring them out from the land of Egypt.” The translation understands the infinitive construct (“to bring them out”) as indicating manner. God’s deliverance of his people from Egypt was an act of self-revelation in that it displayed his power and his commitment to his promises.

verses.zh: 这样，我就使他们出埃及地，领他们到旷野，
verses.en: “‘So I brought them out of the land of Egypt and led them to the wilderness.

verses.zh: 将我的律例赐给他们，将我的典章指示他们；人若遵行就必因此活着。
verses.en: I gave them my statutes[NOTE:1] and revealed my regulations to them. The one[NOTE:2] who carries[NOTE:3] them out will live by them![NOTE:4]
notes: The laws were given at Mount Sinai.
Heb “the man.”
Heb “does.”
The wording and the concept are contained in Lev 18:5 and Deut 30:15-19.

verses.zh: 又将我的安息日赐给他们，好在我与他们中间为证据，使他们知道我―耶和华是叫他们成为圣的。
verses.en: I also gave them my Sabbaths[NOTE:1] as a reminder of our relationship,[NOTE:2] so that they would know that I, the Lord, sanctify them.[NOTE:3]
notes: Ezekiel’s contemporary, Jeremiah, also stressed the importance of obedience to the Sabbath law (Jer 17).
Heb “to become a sign between me and them.”
Or “set them apart.” The last phrase of verse 12 appears to be a citation of Exod 31:13.

verses.zh: 以色列家却在旷野悖逆我，不顺从我的律例，厌弃我的典章（人若遵行就必因此活着），大大干犯我的安息日。「我就说，要在旷野将我的忿怒倾在他们身上，灭绝他们。
verses.en: But the house of Israel rebelled against me in the wilderness; they did not follow my statutes and they rejected my regulations (the one who obeys them will live by them), and they utterly desecrated my Sabbaths. So I decided to pour out[NOTE:1] my rage on them in the wilderness and destroy them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and I said/thought to pour out.”
Heb “to bring them to an end.”

verses.zh: 我却为我名的缘故，没有这样行，免得我的名在我领他们出埃及的列国人眼前被亵渎。
verses.en: I acted for the sake of my reputation, so that I would not be profaned before the nations in whose sight I had brought them out.

verses.zh: 并且我在旷野向他们起誓，必不领他们进入我所赐给他们流奶与蜜之地（那地在万国中是有荣耀的）；
verses.en: I also swore[NOTE:1] to them in the wilderness that I would not bring them to the land I had given them—a land flowing with milk and honey, the most beautiful of all lands.
notes: Heb “I lifted up my hand.”

verses.zh: 因为他们厌弃我的典章，不顺从我的律例，干犯我的安息日，他们的心随从自己的偶像。
verses.en: I did this[NOTE:1] because they rejected my regulations, did not follow my statutes, and desecrated my Sabbaths; for their hearts followed their idols.[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “I did this” are not in the Hebrew text but are supplied for stylistic reasons. Verses 15-16 are one long sentence in the Hebrew text. The translation divides this sentence into two for stylistic reasons.
Heb “for after their idols their heart was going.” The use of the active participle (“was going”) in the Hebrew text draws attention to the ongoing nature of their idolatrous behavior.

verses.zh: 虽然如此，我眼仍顾惜他们，不毁灭他们，不在旷野将他们灭绝净尽。
verses.en: Yet I had pity on[NOTE:1] them and did not destroy them, so I did not make an end of them in the wilderness.
notes: Heb “my eye pitied.”

verses.zh: 「我在旷野对他们的儿女说：不要遵行你们父亲的律例，不要谨守他们的恶规，也不要因他们的偶像玷污自己。
verses.en: “‘But I said to their children[NOTE:1] in the wilderness, “Do not follow the practices of your fathers; do not observe their regulations,[NOTE:2] nor defile yourselves with their idols.
notes: Heb “sons,” reflecting the patriarchal idiom of the culture.
Or “standard of justice.” See Ezek 7:27.

verses.zh: 我是耶和华―你们的　神，你们要顺从我的律例，谨守遵行我的典章，
verses.en: I am the Lord your God; follow my statutes, observe my regulations, and carry them out.

verses.zh: 且以我的安息日为圣。这日在我与你们中间为证据，使你们知道我是耶和华―你们的　神。
verses.en: Treat my Sabbaths as holy[NOTE:1] and they will be a reminder of our relationship,[NOTE:2] and then you will know that I am the Lord your God.”
notes: Or “set apart my Sabbaths.”
Heb “and they will become a sign between me and you.”

verses.zh: 只是他们的儿女悖逆我，不顺从我的律例，也不谨守遵行我的典章（人若遵行就必因此活着），干犯我的安息日。「我就说，要将我的忿怒倾在他们身上，在旷野向他们成就我怒中所定的。
verses.en: But the children[NOTE:1] rebelled against me, did not follow my statutes, did not observe my regulations by carrying them out (the one who obeys[NOTE:2] them will live by them), and desecrated my Sabbaths. I decided to pour out[NOTE:3] my rage on them and fully vent my anger against them in the wilderness.
notes: Heb “sons.”
Or “carries them out.”
Heb “and I said/thought to pour out.”

verses.zh: 虽然如此，我却为我名的缘故缩手没有这样行，免得我的名在我领他们出埃及的列国人眼前被亵渎。
verses.en: But I refrained from doing so[NOTE:1] and acted instead for the sake of my reputation, so that I would not be profaned before the nations in whose sight I had brought them out.
notes: Heb “drew my hand back.” This idiom also occurs in Lam 2:8 and Ps 74:11.

verses.zh: 并且我在旷野向他们起誓，必将他们分散在列国，四散在列邦；
verses.en: I also swore[NOTE:1] to them in the wilderness that I would scatter them among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “I lifted up my hand.”
Though the Pentateuch does not seem to know of this episode, Ps 106:26-27 may speak of God’s oath to exile the people before they had entered Canaan.

verses.zh: 因为他们不遵行我的典章，竟厌弃我的律例，干犯我的安息日，眼目仰望他们父亲的偶像。
verses.en: I did this[NOTE:1] because they did not observe my regulations, they rejected my statutes, they desecrated my Sabbaths, and their eyes were fixed on[NOTE:2] their fathers’ idols.
notes: The words “I did this” are not in the Hebrew text but are supplied for stylistic reasons. Verses 23-24 are one long sentence in the Hebrew text. The translation divides this sentence into two for stylistic reasons.
Or “they worshiped” (NCV, TEV, CEV); Heb “their eyes were on” or “were after” (cf. v. 16).

verses.zh: 我也任他们遵行不美的律例，谨守不能使人活着的恶规。
verses.en: I also gave[NOTE:1] them decrees[NOTE:2] that were not good and regulations by which they could not live.
notes: Or “permitted.” sn The content of the verse is shocking: that God would “give” bad decrees. This probably does not refer to the Mosaic law but to the practices of the Canaanites who were left in the land in order to test Israel. See Judg 2:20-23, the note on “decrees” here in Ezek 20:25, and the note on “pass through the fire” in v. 26.

The Hebrew term חֻקּוֹת (khuqqot; translated “statutes” elsewhere in this chapter) is normally feminine. Here Ezekiel changes the form to masculine: חֻקִּים (khuqqim). Further, they are not called “my decrees” as vv. 11 and 13 refer to “my statutes.” The change is a signal that Ezekiel is not talking about the same statutes in vv. 11 and 13, which lead to life.

verses.zh: 因他们将一切头生的经火，我就任凭他们在这供献的事上玷污自己，好叫他们凄凉，使他们知道我是耶和华。
verses.en: I declared them to be defiled because of their sacrifices[NOTE:1]—they caused all their firstborn to pass through the fire[NOTE:2]—so that I might devastate them, so that they would know that I am the Lord.’[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “gifts.”

This act is prohibited in Deut 12:29-31 and Jer 7:31; 19:5; 32:35. See also 2 Kgs 21:6; 23:10. This custom indicates that the laws the Israelites were following were the disastrous laws of pagan nations (see Ezek 16:20-21).

God sometimes punishes sin by inciting the sinner to sin even more, as the biblical examples of divine hardening and deceit make clear. See Robert B. Chisholm, Jr., “Divine Hardening in the Old Testament,” BSac 153 (1996): 410-34; idem, “Does God Deceive?” BSac 155 (1998): 11-28. For other instances where the Lord causes individuals to act unwisely or even sinfully as punishment for sin, see 1 Sam 2:25; 2 Sam 17:14; 1 Kgs 12:15; 2 Chr 25:20.

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要告诉以色列家说，主耶和华如此说：你们的列祖在得罪我的事上亵渎我；
verses.en: “Therefore, speak to the house of Israel, son of man, and tell them, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: In this way too your fathers blasphemed me when they were unfaithful to me.

verses.zh: 因为我领他们到了我起誓应许赐给他们的地，他们看见各高山、各茂密树，就在那里献祭，奉上惹我发怒的供物，也在那里焚烧馨香的祭牲，并浇上奠祭。
verses.en: I brought them to the land that I swore[NOTE:1] to give them, but whenever they saw any high hill or leafy tree, they offered their sacrifices there and presented the offerings that provoked me to anger. They offered their soothing aroma there and poured out their drink offerings.
notes: Heb “that I lifted up my hand.”

verses.zh: 我就对他们说：你们所上的那高处叫甚么呢？（那高处的名字叫巴麻直到今日。）
verses.en: So I said to them, “What is this high place you go to?”’ (So it is called “High Place”[NOTE:1] to this day.)
notes: The Hebrew word בָּמָה (bamah) means “high place.”

verses.zh: 所以你要对以色列家说，主耶和华如此说：你们仍照你们列祖所行的玷污自己吗？仍照他们可憎的事行邪淫吗？
verses.en: “Therefore say to the house of Israel, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: Will you defile yourselves like your fathers[NOTE:1] and engage in prostitution with detestable idols?
notes: Heb “in the way of your fathers.”

verses.zh: 你们奉上供物使你们儿子经火的时候，仍将一切偶像玷污自己，直到今日吗？以色列家啊，我岂被你们求问吗？主耶和华说：我指着我的永生起誓，我必不被你们求问。
verses.en: When you present your sacrifices[NOTE:1]—when you make your sons pass through the fire—you defile yourselves with all your idols to this very day. Will I allow you to seek me,[NOTE:2] O house of Israel? As surely as I live, declares the Sovereign Lord, I will not allow you to seek me![NOTE:3]
notes: Or “gifts.”
Or “Will I reveal myself to you?”
Or “I will not reveal myself to you.”

verses.zh: 「你们说：我们要像外邦人和列国的宗族一样，去事奉木头与石头。你们所起的这心意万不能成就。」
verses.en: “‘What you plan[NOTE:1] will never happen. You say, “We will be[NOTE:2] like the nations, like the clans of the lands, who serve gods of wood and stone.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “what comes upon your mind.”
The Hebrew could also read: “Let us be.”
Heb “serving wood and stone.” sn This verse echoes the content of 1 Sam 8:20.

verses.zh: 主耶和华说：「我指着我的永生起誓，我总要作王，用大能的手和伸出来的膀臂，并倾出来的忿怒，治理你们。
verses.en: As surely as I live, declares the Sovereign Lord, with a powerful hand and an outstretched arm[NOTE:1] and with an outpouring of rage, I will be king over you.
notes: This phrase occurs frequently in Deuteronomy (Deut 4:34; 5:15; 7:19; 11:2; 26:8).

verses.zh: 我必用大能的手和伸出来的膀臂，并倾出来的忿怒，将你们从万民中领出来，从分散的列国内聚集你们。
verses.en: I will bring you out from the nations and will gather you from the lands where you are scattered, with a powerful hand and an outstretched arm and with an outpouring of rage!

verses.zh: 我必带你们到外邦人的旷野，在那里当面刑罚你们。
verses.en: I will bring you into the wilderness of the nations, and there I will enter into judgment with you face-to-face.

verses.zh: 我怎样在埃及地的旷野刑罚你们的列祖，也必照样刑罚你们。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: Just as I entered into judgment with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so I will enter into judgment with you, declares the Sovereign Lord.

verses.zh: 我必使你们从杖下经过，使你们被约拘束。
verses.en: I will make you pass under[NOTE:1] the shepherd’s staff,[NOTE:2] and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant.
notes: This is the same Hebrew verb used to describe the passing of the children through the fire.
The metaphor may be based in Lev 27:32 (see also Jer 33:13 and Matt 25:32-33). A shepherd would count his sheep as they passed beneath his staff.

verses.zh: 我必从你们中间除净叛逆和得罪我的人，将他们从所寄居的地方领出来，他们却不得入以色列地。你们就知道我是耶和华。
verses.en: I will eliminate from among you the rebels and those who revolt[NOTE:1] against me. I will bring them out from the land where they have been residing, but they will not come to the land of Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
notes: See the note at 2:3.

verses.zh: 「以色列家啊，至于你们，主耶和华如此说：从此以后若不听从我，就任凭你们去事奉偶像，只是不可再因你们的供物和偶像亵渎我的圣名。
verses.en: “‘As for you, O house of Israel, this is what the Sovereign Lord says: Each of you go and serve your idols,[NOTE:1] if you will not listen to me.[NOTE:2] But my holy name will not be profaned[NOTE:3] again by your sacrifices[NOTE:4] and your idols.
notes: Compare the irony here to Amos 4:4 and Jer 44:25.

Heb “and after, if you will not listen to me.” The translation leaves out “and after” for smoothness. The text is difficult. M. Greenberg (Ezekiel [AB], 1:374) suggests that it may mean “but afterwards, if you will not listen to me…” with an unspoken threat.
A similar concept may be found in Lev 18:21 and 20:3.
Or “gifts.”

verses.zh: 「主耶和华说：在我的圣山，就是以色列高处的山，所有以色列的全家都要事奉我。我要在那里悦纳你们，向你们要供物和初熟的土产，并一切的圣物。
verses.en: For there on my holy mountain, the high mountain of Israel, declares the Sovereign Lord, all the house of Israel will serve me, all of them[NOTE:1] in the land. I will accept them there, and there I will seek your contributions and your choice gifts, with all your holy things.
notes: Heb “all of it.”

verses.zh: 我从万民中领你们出来，从分散的列国内聚集你们，那时我必悦纳你们好像馨香之祭，要在外邦人眼前在你们身上显为圣。
verses.en: When I bring you out from the nations and gather you from the lands where you are scattered, I will accept you along with your soothing aroma. I will display my holiness among you in the sight of the nations.

verses.zh: 我领你们进入以色列地，就是我起誓应许赐给你们列祖之地，那时你们就知道我是耶和华。
verses.en: Then you will know that I am the Lord when I bring you to the land of Israel, to the land I swore[NOTE:1] to give to your fathers.
notes: Heb “I lifted up my hand.”

verses.zh: 你们在那里要追念玷污自己的行动作为，又要因所做的一切恶事厌恶自己。
verses.en: And there you will remember your conduct[NOTE:1] and all your deeds by which you defiled yourselves. You will despise yourselves[NOTE:2] because of all the evil deeds you have done.
notes: Heb “ways.”
Heb “loathe yourselves in your faces.”

verses.zh: 主耶和华说：以色列家啊，我为我名的缘故，不照着你们的恶行和你们的坏事待你们；你们就知道我是耶和华。」
verses.en: Then you will know that I am the Lord, when I deal with you for the sake of my reputation and not according to your wicked conduct and corrupt deeds, O house of Israel, declares the Sovereign Lord.’”

verses.zh: 耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: (21:1)[NOTE:1] The Lord’s message came to me:
notes: Beginning with 20:45, the verse numbers through 21:32 in the English Bible differ by five from the verse numbers in the Hebrew text (BHS), with 20:45 ET = 21:1 HT, 20:46 ET = 21:2 HT, 21:1 ET = 21:6 HT etc., through 21:32 ET = 21:37 HT. Beginning with 22:1 the verse numbers in the English Bible and the Hebrew Bible are again the same.

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要面向南方，向南滴下预言攻击南方田野的树林。
verses.en: “Son of man, turn toward[NOTE:1] the south,[NOTE:2] and speak out against the south.[NOTE:3] Prophesy against the open scrub[NOTE:4] land of the Negev,
notes: Heb “set your face toward.” This expression occurs as well in Ezek 6:2 and 13:17.
Or “the way toward the south,” or “the way toward Teman.” Teman is in the south and may be a location or the direction.
Or “toward Darom.” Darom may mean the south or a region just north of the southern city of Beer Sheba. See M. Greenberg, Ezekiel (AB), 2:417-18.
The Hebrew term can also mean “forest,” but a meaning of uncultivated wasteland fits the Negev region far better. See M. Greenberg, Ezekiel (AB), 2:418.

verses.zh: 对南方的树林说，要听耶和华的话。主耶和华如此说：我必使火在你中间着起，烧灭你中间的一切青树和枯树，猛烈的火焰必不熄灭。从南到北，人的脸面都被烧焦。
verses.en: and say to the scrub land of the Negev, ‘Listen to the Lord’s message! This is what the Sovereign Lord has said: Look here,[NOTE:1] I am about to start a fire in you,[NOTE:2] and it will devour every green tree and every dry tree in you. The flaming fire will not be extinguished, and the whole surface of the ground from the Negev to the north will be scorched by it.
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.
Fire also appears as a form of judgment in Ezek 15:4-7 and 19:12, 14.

verses.zh: 凡有血气的都必知道是我―耶和华使火着起，这火必不熄灭。」
verses.en: And everyone[NOTE:1] will see that I, the Lord, have burned it; it will not be extinguished.’”
notes: Heb “all flesh.”

verses.zh: 于是我说：「哎！主耶和华啊，人都指着我说：他岂不是说比喻的吗？」
verses.en: Then I said, “O Sovereign Lord! They are saying of me, ‘Does he not simply speak in eloquent figures of speech?’”
